caption: Luke deliberately reuses the “horn of salvation” image for Jesus in David’s house. Psalm 18 originally uses it for God while celebrating a past rescue.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 18 call Jesus salvation’s horn? David calls God the horn of his salvation. Luke says God raised a horn of salvation in David’s family.
slides.body: David calls God the horn of his salvation. Luke says God raised a horn of salvation in David’s family.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 18 call Jesus salvation’s horn?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 18:2-3: The LORD is … the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
slides.body: The LORD is … the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
slides.heading: Ps 18:2-3

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Lk 1:69–71, BSB: He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David … salvation from our enemies.
slides.body: He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David … salvation from our enemies.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Lk 1:69–71

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The phrase is deliberately reused Both passages celebrate rescue from enemies. Luke presents Jesus as the promised Davidic agent of God’s salvation.
slides.body: Both passages celebrate rescue from enemies. Luke presents Jesus as the promised Davidic agent of God’s salvation.
slides.heading: The phrase is deliberately reused

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the psalm calls God the horn It praises a rescue already received and predicts no future child. Luke gives the old image a new focus.
slides.body: It praises a rescue already received and predicts no future child. Luke gives the old image a new focus.
slides.heading: But the psalm calls God the horn

title: The horn of salvation
